animations.title: Search bar: focus and the go arrow
animations.trigger: tap the field; type the first letter
animations.now: No focus style at all. On the first letter the 36px copper go arrow appears and the mic and clip jump 42px left - all in one frame; clearing reverses it in one frame.
animations.verdict: Focus is a color change (exempt, 120ms). The arrow is the primary action appearing: a quick deep-scale entrance. Hiding on clear stays instant - it follows the keys.
animations.notes: Today: .fam-input-box (249) has no :focus-within rule and the textarea has outline:none, so the only sign of focus on a phone is the keyboard rising. Next-up's search (2869) turns its border copper on focus - the search bar should match it (Similarity). paintSearchBar (7197) sets go.hidden from the value on every input event, so the arrow appears with the first letter and disappears when the box is emptied; go is added at the right of .bar-btns, so the mic and attach jump 42px left in the same frame (measured: mic x 283 to 241 at 390 wide) - the brief's 'mic swaps to a send arrow' is option C, not today. The .tall reflow (a question past one line) and trending hiding on the first keystroke are keyboard-driven and must stay instant (Frequency of use). Option A: border-color transition 120ms ease on :focus-within, put on the focus rule only so a keyboard focus is not delayed by more than the color. The arrow: render it always, toggle a data-state, and run the icon-swap recipe (scale .3 to 1, opacity, blur 3px to 0) over 260ms (.32,.72,0,1); origin centre. Its exit when cleared is instant (backspace is the keyboard). Interrupt: typing a letter, deleting it and typing again mid-entrance turns around from where it is because it is a transition, not a keyframe. The press squeeze still applies when the arrow is tapped. Option C is a layout change for the owner (rule search-bar says mic and attach inside the bar's right; that stays true while the box is empty). Today the mic with words typed opens an empty sheet and sending replaces the typed words, so losing the mic while typing costs little. Reduced motion: everything changes on the same frame. Verify: Tenth use - a 260ms pop seen 30 times a day; cut to 200ms if it feels slow.

animations.title: The loading screen arrives
animations.trigger: send a search, a trending search, a Go Deeper or a voice search
animations.now: The full-screen loader appears in one frame (display none to flex) - up to 700ms after the press while /api/spell answers. Its X (cancel) removes it in one frame.
animations.verdict: Few a session and full-screen: a 220ms fade is in budget. Show it on the press, not after the speller; leave as an inert copy in 160ms. Nothing here delays a step.
animations.notes: Today: generate() (8393) adds .active and .fam-loading.active (2175) is display:flex - a cut. Before that, runSearch (7074) may wait up to AC_SEND_WAIT_MS 700ms on acCorrectQuestion with searchSending set and nothing new drawn: after the press squeeze there is no answer for up to 0.7s (Doherty). Opening the loader on the press is honest - step one, 'Contextualizing your search', is literally what the speller is doing - and holds nothing: startGenSteps' 0.5s first-step floor should still count from the request, so the first check can only be later, never earlier. Edge: the AI-consent question (withAiConsent) may still need to appear; open the loader after consent is known, or close it before the consent modal. Exit: cancelGeneration (7687) and failures call clearGenOverlay, which cuts. With an inert copy (Motion's pattern) the real overlay is gone on frame one and the copy fades, so the search page is live at once. The 'Cancelled' bottom line should start as the copy lands (Staging). Voice send: the loader fades in over the voice sheet, and the sheet is hidden under it, so search never flashes. Option B's wordmark glide is short (search's FAM logo sits ~28px above the loader's at 390x844; the loader's is ~23% wider); the five rows stagger 40ms (copies of one element), all in by ~400ms, inside step one's 0.5s floor. Option C adds the typed question to the loading screen: new content, so it is the owner's call; it answers 'what is it making?' but the loader has been kept spare (232 removed the seconds). Reduced motion: the loader appears and leaves on one frame (A, B, C), and still opens on the press. Never: a delay before the loader shows (it would be a hold), or a longer fade - Tenth use at 220ms is fine.

animations.title: The five steps check off
animations.trigger: the server's mark for a step (each held 2s, the first 0.5s)
animations.now: Row: opacity .55→1 and color over .35s ease. Dot: copper fill .3s ease. Tick: opacity .25s, scale .4→1 .3s cubic-bezier(.3,1.6,.5,1) (peaks ~1.07). Next dot pulses a box-shadow.
animations.verdict: Restyle only - the timing is product. Drop the overshoot (routine, not a milestone), draw the tick like Follow's, ring on transform/opacity, finish inside the 400ms last beat.
animations.notes: Decided behaviour, untouched by every option: each check lands only on the server's mark (/api/progress), each step is on screen at least GEN_STEP_MIN_MS 2000 (first GEN_STEP_FIRST_MIN_MS 500), audio is held until the fifth check, then GEN_STEP_LAST_BEAT_MS 400 before it starts; a replay paints all five done at once. So the fifth check's animation must be complete within 400ms or the screen leaves on a half-drawn tick: A lands at 300ms, B's tick at 300ms (its rail is not drawn after step 5), C at 220ms. Today (2238-2257): li transition opacity .35s ease, color .35s ease; dot background/border .3s ease; svg opacity .25s ease and transform .3s cubic-bezier(.3,1.6,.5,1) from scale(.4) - the y1 of 1.6 overshoots, which the skill keeps out of product UI; famStepPulse animates box-shadow, which repaints. A: give the check path pathLength=1 and stroke-dasharray 1, and transition stroke-dashoffset 1 to 0 over 220ms, 80ms after the fill - the numbers of the owner's Follow tick (Motion.follow, 6573), so a finished thing is drawn the same way across the app. The ring moves to li.active .fam-step-dot::after (see 'The loader's moving mark' for its clock). paintGenSteps toggles classes, so everything is a transition and a replay's all-done paint jumps straight to the end state (no five ticks in a row). B adds a 2px copper rail between dots (an element per gap, scaleY from the top) - Uniform connectedness: five rows read as one path, and the filled length is how far along the work is (goal gradient). It never suggests a step is done before its mark: the segment fills only after the tick. C is today's look, cleaned. Reduced motion (all): dot fills and tick shows on one frame; the active ring keeps an opacity-only pulse - the progress-indicator exception - so the screen never looks hung. Interrupt: a cancel mid-tick removes the overlay copy; nothing to turn around.

animations.title: The loader's moving mark
animations.now: Three chevrons rise 11px and fade, 2.4s (.4,0,.2,1) loop, 0/.22/.44s apart; the active dot pulses box-shadow 0→5px, 1.6s ease-in-out. Reduced motion stops both.
animations.verdict: Two loops on two clocks split the eye, and box-shadow repaints. Lock both to one beat, ring on transform/opacity, and under reduced motion keep one indicator moving.
animations.notes: The chevrons (2192) are HTML layers since 288 so the compositor moves them while the page is busy - keep that. famRise: 0% y+11 opacity 0, 20% in place, 62% hold, 100% y-11 opacity 0; c2 and c3 start .22s and .44s later, so c3 lands at .44+.48 = .92s of every 2.4s cycle. famStepPulse (2253) runs a 1.6s box-shadow ring on li.active .fam-step-dot. Two periods (2.4s, 1.6s) drift against each other: the eye has two things to follow (Staging), and box-shadow is painted each frame (Properties). Reduced motion (2346) sets both to animation:none: for 8.5s or more the screen is completely still, which the skill names as the one exception - a progress indicator keeps moving. Phase-locking in A: the ring is a 2.4s animation on ::after (0% scale 1 opacity 0; 38% opacity .5; 88% scale 1.7 opacity 0); it starts whenever a row becomes active, so set its startTime to the chevrons' (WAAPI anim.startTime = chev.getAnimations()[0].startTime) or a negative animation-delay of (now - loaderStart) mod 2400. B moves the chevrons to a rAF sine - truly seamless and one clock, but 288 moved them OFF the main thread because they stalled while an episode starts; B would bring that back unless written as WAAPI keyframes sampled from a sine (12 stops), which is the build note if B is picked. C stills the chevrons only on search's stepped loader; Play All's 'Writing your episodes...' keeps them. famDot (dots) is hidden on search (.stepped) and famLdUp/famLdPulse belong to dailyFAM's and myFAM's loaders - not this page. Under reduced motion every option keeps the ring as opacity .35 to 1, 1.2s ease-in-out alternate, and the chevrons still.

Inside it: showThreadSuggestion (9067) first draws the title-built line ('Follow the thread' - What's the bigger story behind X?), and fetchEpisodeThread / openGoDeeperOn replace it with the writer's <<NEXT:>> line ('Pick up the thread') whenever it lands - often while the box is open, because the episode is still being written. animations.now: While speaking, arcs pulse scale 1→1+lvl·0.09 (lines scaleX 1+lvl·0.35), 1.1s ease-in-out loop, 0/.18/.36s delays; opacity follows lvl over .35s. Below lvl .08 scale snaps to 1.
animations.verdict: Keep 'moves only while somebody talks'. Drive it from the rAF loop that exists, as a sine with phases on the 8 paths, so it settles instead of snapping.
animations.notes: The rule (151 comment at 11467): the lines move because somebody is talking, driven by the recogniser's speech and result events, so a silent room shows a still mark. Keep it. Today voiceLevelLoop (11595) runs every frame while the sheet is open: lvl *= 0.93, writes --lvl on the whole #voiceSearch (every descendant restyles - the skill's 'never animate a custom property read deep in a tree'), and toggles .speaking when lvl > .08. A result sets lvl to 1; it falls below .08 after ~35 frames (~580ms). .speaking adds the vs-wave keyframes; removing the class removes the animation, so the arcs jump to scale 1 mid-pulse while their opacity fades over .35s - a seam each time speech pauses (keyframes on a toggle). Also var(--lvl) inside @keyframes: live updates are unverified on iPhone Safari. A: in the same loop, compute each path's transform from a sine with a phase per ring (0, .16, .33 cycles - phase, not delay) and amplitude lvl, write style.transform and opacity on the 8 paths only; as lvl decays the motion shrinks to rest smoothly; stop the loop when not listening and lvl is ~0 (battery), restart on speech. B is a different metaphor: each result event (throttled to one per 150ms) emits one ring from the mark - honest per event, but busy when results stream, and it drops the arcs the owner approved. C keeps keyframes always running with amplitude on .vs-waves, so a pause fades the amplitude rather than removing the animation. Reduced motion: no scaling; the arcs' opacity still follows lvl (an indicator that it is hearing you), changing without a transition.

animations.title: Which one do you mean?
animations.trigger: the server finds an ambiguous name; tap 'Type your own'
animations.now: The loader vanishes in one frame as the modal fades and lifts in (200ms). 'Type your own' becomes the field in one frame (hidden swap, same 46px slot). A choice cuts back to the loader.
animations.verdict: A question in the middle of a wait: hand off from the loader without a flash of search, and swap the pill for the field in place, in one grid cell.
animations.notes: Flow: the search's loader is up (step 1 active); the server answers with readings (426); onGenerationFailed (7706) calls clearGenOverlay - a cut to the search page - then askReading adds .active to #readingOverlay (shared modal fade-and-lift, 200ms). So for one frame the listener is back on search, then a modal. A: let the loader's inert copy fade 160ms ease-in on the same frame the modal starts, so the eye goes loader to question. Choosing a reading calls generate, whose loader should fade in (see 'The loading screen arrives') as the modal drops (150ms, shared). 'Type your own' (.reading-own, 2512) and the field row (.reading-own-row, 2514) are both 46px min-height with 8px top margin - a perfect replacement slot: put both in one grid cell, pill fades + scales to .97 (150ms ease-in) while the row fades in from .97 (200ms ease-out); the send arrow (disabled until text) enters with the icon-swap scale .3 to 1. Focus is set on the same frame so the keyboard rises at once (never wait for the animation). B makes the pill and field one object (dashed border cross-fades to solid copper, label slides into the placeholder) - nicer, fussy for a rare moment. C moves the question onto the loader itself: step 1 'Contextualizing your search' is exactly where the server stopped, so its row opens (grid-rows 250ms ease-in-out) to hold the choices and closes when one is picked, the steps carrying on - honest and modal-free, but a layout change for the owner. Cancel: today returns to an empty bar (the question was cleared at send) - see findings. Reduced motion: loader goes and the field appears on one frame.

animations.title: An attachment: read, failed, removed
animations.trigger: pick a file or link; the server reads it; tap x
animations.now: The chip appears in one frame at 60% opacity with 'reading...' and nothing moves for seconds; done or failed swap in one frame (coral + a toast); x removes it in one frame.
animations.verdict: Rare, so it may be choreographed. A read that takes seconds needs a moving indicator; a failure may register once; a removal leaves with the gap closing.
animations.notes: sendAttachment (6995) pushes a pending slot and renderAttachments (6929) rewrites #attachRow's innerHTML on every change - so nothing can transition; render by key instead (one element per slot, updated in place). Pending is .attach-chip.working (opacity .6) with 'reading...': a PDF can take seconds, and a still, faded chip looks like it stalled (Doherty: work that takes seconds is never a bare wait; this one is not even moving). A's bar is a 2px copper strip clipped to the chip's bottom edge, translateX -100% to 100%, 1.2s linear, infinite - a progress indicator, so it keeps moving under reduced motion. Failure (.failed, coral, 403) plus a toast: an error shake is the skill's one sanctioned exaggeration for a failed attempt (translateX 0,-6,6,-3,3,0 over 300ms, smaller than the field's 10px because a chip is small), once, with the message already in the chip. Removal: the x is a 13px glyph in a span (401) - make it a button with a 44px ::after; the chip leaves as an inert copy (opacity, scale .95, 150ms ease-in) and the other chips close the gap with FLIP 200ms ease-in-out. removeAttachment (6948) DELETEs at once with no Undo; the skill's rule is remove from view now, delete when a 5s Undo window closes. Side effects to keep instant: trending hides while anything is attached, and the go arrow appears (see 'Search bar: focus and the go arrow'). B adds Origin and Arcs (a glyph flies from the clip into the chip) - 560ms of choreography is allowed for a rare action, slow for someone attaching three. C is Occam's razor: only the wait moves. Reduced motion: chips appear and leave at once; the reading bar keeps moving; no shake (the coral and the words carry the failure).
